Ben —

Appreciate the detail. I attached a concise proposal (sealed-update-proposal.pdf) that outlines a four-stage sealed-update workflow we recommend for air-gapped sites. High level:

1) Build & sign: Redwood produces the release bundle; if the customer provides an HSM signing key we cross-sign (recommended). Otherwise we publish a Redwood-signed artifact and a secondary customer signature step. Use COSE/PEM envelopes and include sha256 checksums.

2) Produce a signed manifest: manifest.json contains artifacts, checksums, signatures, build metadata, and a monotonic sequence number. The manifest is signed by the final authority (customer HSM ideally).

3) Transfer & verify: transfer via transfer-box (removable media). On the transfer host, run the verification script that checks signature envelopes and checksums before making the artifact available to the cluster update broker. Audit logs are exported to a write-once location.

4) Apply & monitor: staged rollout to a sealed staging cluster (identical to prod), smoke tests run, then maintenance window for production. Rollback implemented via artifact pinning and a fast-rollback script that reverts to previous image and clears KV cache if necessary.

Attachments in the proposal: sample manifest, an example verification command set, and a short runbook.

Open items I flagged in the doc:
- Customer HSM options and exact signature format you prefer (PKCS#11 / YubiHSM / cloud-HSM export rules).
- Your allowed checksum algorithms.
- Acceptable maintenance windows.

Next step: Soojin and Dev will add the low-level signing and deploy steps, plus a mitigation runbook. If this looks right to you we can convert to your change-control format and produce an ingestion example.

Ben / team —

Quick technical notes from sign-off perspective (see image-signing-checklist.md attached):
- Signing: we recommend cosign-style signatures (RFC-like envelope) with sha256 and timestamp. For highest assurance, dual-signature: Redwood key + customer HSM key. The customer key should sign the manifest; Redwood signs the artifact layer. Verification validates both signatures before acceptance.
- Manifest format: JSON with fields: sequence, artifacts [{path, sha256, size}], signatures [{key_id, signature}], provenance {build_id, git_commit}. Keep manifest size small and text-only to ease offline transport.
- Verification chain: verification script will check signature(s), confirm checksum, then compute a short-lived local attestation (signed statement from the transfer host) that the artifact was verified on a hardened transfer box. That attestation is recorded in the update broker ledger.
- If HSM not available: customer can supply an approved signing operator key that is cross-signed by their root; we list acceptable key handling in the checklist.

Also: we should include a small acceptance test harness that runs two smoke probes (API ping + KV consistency) before approving the update. See attached: image-signing-checklist.md.

—Soojin
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben, Hannah —

Sharing a trimmed playbook excerpt and some pragmatic checks (I attached scoped-mitigation-runbook.txt):
- Pre-step (on build farm): produce release tarball, generate sha256sum and sign artifact with cosign. Publish artifact and manifest in an offline bundle (tar.gz).
- Transfer step: write bundle to hardware-encrypted transfer drive; checksum the drive image; create transfer-log.txt with hardware serial; have two operators sign the transfer-log (physical signatures required).
- Verification step on transfer host: ./verify-manifest.sh manifest.json --trust-roots /opt/trust-roots/ ; if verify passes, move artifact to /var/lib/redwood/incoming and trigger update-broker service which performs staged extraction.
- Staged update: staged namespace -> run smoke harness (./smoke-run.sh) -> if success promote to prod namespace. If failure, run ./rollback-pin.sh <previous-sequence>.

Network notes: keep the update-broker host isolated with only outbound SMB to local NFS for artifact staging; no DNS resolution required during verification stage. Ensure the transfer host is power-cycled and scanned by the airgap scanner before connecting.

I'll produce an automation tarball with the verify scripts and the smoke harness — expect that Monday.
